chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ja'far ibn Uthman, who said:

My father carried goods to Syria with a cameleer, and mentioned that one load from it was lost. So I mentioned that to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him). He said: 'Did you accuse him?' I said: 'No'. He said: 'So do not hold him liable (guarantee the loss).'

key_terms.تُضَمِّنْهُ: Hold him liable / Guarantee the loss

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on compensating a transporter for lost goods in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies the default state of *daman* (liability) for hired transporters, ruling that loss without proven negligence does not incur compensation. This establishes the principle of *al-‘asl fi al-daman al-barā’ah* (the default is exemption from liability) unless fault is demonstrated, a cornerstone of Shia commercial jurisprudence. The ruling emphasizes fairness by preventing unjust accusations against the worker for unforeseen losses during transit.
